drivingQuestion: Does wine, like bread, require reclining before one person may bless on behalf of the whole company?
outcomeNote: The dispute is recorded and not decided here; a second version of Rav's statement, with objections, follows in the next unit.

segments.he: הֵסַבּוּ, אֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ. אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פַּת דְּבָעֵי הֲסִבָּה, אֲבָל יַיִן לָא בָּעֵי הֲסִבָּה. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן נָמֵי בָּעֵי הֲסִבָּה.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «If they were reclined, one recites a blessing» on behalf of them all. «Rav said: This» halakha «was only taught» with regard to «bread that» it «requires reclining» to enable one to recite a blessing on behalf of them all. «However, wine does not require reclining. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even wine requires reclining as well.»

moves.summary: the mishna's clause on reclining is quoted as the lemma
moves.about: the mishna's clause that when they reclined, one blesses for all

moves.cueHe: אמר רב: לא שנו אלא פת דבעי הסבה
moves.summary: Rav confines the requirement of reclining to bread
moves.about: the mishna's requirement of reclining was taught only of bread; wine needs no reclining for one to bless for all

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוחנן אמר: אפילו יין נמי בעי הסבה
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan holds that wine too requires reclining
moves.about: whether wine, like bread, requires reclining before one person may bless on behalf of all
